description: Verifies the receipt at the end of one response against the text before it. It takes no physics permit. The receipt covers every byte of the response before it, the decimal values included, and shows who produced the response or when in no way: it has no key. matches true proves only that those bytes are unchanged since the receipt was written; anyone can write a matching receipt for any text, so it is not a verification of the answer. A response that names an engine_version has it said beside matches, with whether it is this engine's; origin needs engine_version_is_this_engines true and a replay. match_proves says this in each answer. The receipt covers the request as it was written, number spellings included, while a seal covers its values: a request sent with 310 and the same request sent with 310.0 give different receipts and the same seal, so a receipt that differs between two such answers is not a sign of tampering. Replaying the request through run_trajectory, solve or compute_step shows the engine produced it; verify_tape, verify_solution and verify_dataset with the request and its seal do that replay and compare the seals.

inputSchema.description: The text of one response from compute_step, run_trajectory or solve, or the head of a dataset written as its JSON text. A signature after the receipt is checked against public_key or else this engine's own key, and reported under signature.

public_key.description: The base64 of the ML-DSA-87 public key (2,592 bytes) to check the answer's signature with; without it, this engine's own.

response_text.description: The exact text of a response as it was received, ending with the receipt, and the engine's signature after it when it carries one.

seen_nonces.description: Nonces of signatures already seen: one of them again is SignatureNonceReplayed.

name: verify_receipt
title: Verify receipt
